area: Testing & visual regression — what is genuinely additive on top of the 55/55 fidelity gate

item_verdicts.title: Run the existing ?fidelity=auto gate headlessly in CI via a Playwright script
item_verdicts.why: Every repo-side claim verified: src/main.ts gates `__fidelity` + `__fidelityAuto` behind `import.meta.env.DEV`, writes a 'running' marker then a compact verdict (pass/points/scans/failed/failures) to localStorage; `git ls-files` confirms src/config/fidelity.ts and src/game/fidelity.ts are TRACKED while `reference/` is line 8 of .gitignore, so gate data ships with the repo; .github/workflows/ci.yml runs only `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `npm run build` — no browser step, so the gate really does regress silently; FIDELITY_GATE.md documents the manual `game.loop.step()` rAF-throttle fallback and the 60-120 s throttled runtime. The SwiftShader flag requirement is real: the Chromium doc gives `--enable-unsafe-swiftshader` and says 'Allowing automatic fallback to WebGL backed by SwiftShader has been deprecated and WebGL context creation will soon fail instead of falling back to SwiftShader' — but names NO version, and the cited chromestatus entry (fetched raw via its API: name 'Remove SwiftShader fallback', status 'Deprecated', milestone_str '139', desktop 139, first_enterprise_notification_milestone 131) contradicts 'starting Chrome 130'. Also: neither playwright nor @playwright/test is in package.json today, so this item adds a devDependency plus a browser download.
item_verdicts.correction: Replace 'because Chromium deprecated the automatic SwiftShader fallback starting Chrome 130' with: 'because Chromium removed the automatic SwiftShader fallback — chromestatus feature 5166674414927872 ("Remove SwiftShader fallback") lists desktop milestone 139, enterprise notification from 131; the Chromium SwiftShader doc states the deprecation without naming a version. Any current CI Chromium is past 139, so --enable-unsafe-swiftshader is mandatory on GPU-less runners.' Also note Playwright is not yet a dependency: `npm i -D playwright` + `npx playwright install chromium` is part of the cost.

item_verdicts.title: Full-canvas pixelmatch baselines per canonical gate state — the regression net between the 55 points
item_verdicts.why: The coverage-gap core is CONFIRMED and is stronger than stated: the live config has FIDELITY_PROBES = 40 and FIDELITY_SCANS = 14, and src/game/fidelity.ts pushes ONE runtime-built probe ('enemy-bar-green', anchored to sim.enemy.pos) = exactly the documented 41 points + 14 scans = 55. Every fighting-state probe id is HUD chrome (plate-fill, hp/chi bar ends + gradients, focus-strip, portrait-ring, slot interiors, slot-border-top) — ZERO probes on the fighter body, so a SESSION-19-class art bug is genuinely invisible to the gate. The five states in the harness (vs-intro, fight-splash, fighting, result-win, result-defeat — the last two via scene.launch inside a storage backup/restore) match the item's list, and DuelIntro.devHoldAt exists. Environment-pinning is well sourced: Playwright docs say screenshots differ between browsers and platforms and to 'run tests in the same environment where the baseline screenshots were generated'; the Vitest guide requires 'a standardized and tightly controlled environment'. Both confirm pixelmatch as the default/built-in comparator. One factual error: pixelmatch no longer uses a YIQ metric — current pixelmatch uses OKLab with the HyAB metric (threshold default 0.1 ✓, includeAA default false ✓, diff image with diffColor red / aaColor yellow ✓), and Vitest's own defaults differ (threshold 0.2 + allowedMismatchedPixelRatio).
item_verdicts.correction: Change 'threshold ~0.1 YIQ/perceptual metric' to: 'threshold default 0.1, perceptual difference computed in OKLab with the HyAB metric (pixelmatch v7 — YIQ was the pre-v6 metric); Vitest's built-in comparator defaults to threshold 0.2 plus allowedMismatchedPixelRatio, so choose the numbers explicitly rather than inheriting them.' Also state precisely that 41 points = 40 committed FIDELITY_PROBES + 1 runtime probe (enemy-bar-green) built in src/game/fidelity.ts, and that the fighting state has no fighter-body probe at all — that is the gap this item closes.

item_verdicts.title: Vitest 4 browser mode + toMatchScreenshot as the screenshot harness
item_verdicts.why: Both the factual claim and the REJECT reasoning survive. Sources: the Vitest 4.0 blog does say 'we are removing the experimental tag from Browser Mode' and demonstrates `await expect(page.getByTestId('hero')).toMatchScreenshot('hero-section')'; the visual-regression guide confirms pixelmatch as the shipped comparator and 'Stable Screenshot Detection'. Repo facts behind the REJECT check out exactly: package.json has "vitest": "^4.1.10"; .githooks/pre-commit sets TEST_CMD="npx vitest run" verbatim (only an all-markdown staged set skips it); src/main.ts already owns the page-level harness (window.__fidelity, window.__game, ?fidelity=auto). One extra fact STRENGTHENS the rejection: Vitest 4 moved the browser provider into a separate package ('you now need to install a separate package: @vitest/browser-playwright'), so this route costs a new dependency AND projects-config fencing for coverage items 1+2 get from the existing seam.

item_verdicts.title: Failure artifacts: dump per-state canvas PNGs (+ diff images) when the CI gate goes red
item_verdicts.why: Verified against src/main.ts: the __fidelityAuto payload is {pass, points, scans, failed, failures[], finishedAt} — compare results only, no image — so a remote red is genuinely undiagnosable without a screenshot, exactly as argued. pixelmatch's README confirms diff-image output ('writes the output diff and returns the number of mismatched pixels', diffColor red / aaColor yellow), and the harness drives every canonical state from outside (scene.launch / devHoldAt), so no src/ change is needed. Minor citation slip, not enough to weaken: the fetched Playwright test-snapshots page does not discuss actual/expected/diff report attachments — irrelevant, since the plan uses page.screenshot() + upload-artifact rather than the Playwright test runner.

item_verdicts.title: Determinism prerequisites for stable screenshots (freeze animations, seed randomness, fixed timestep)
item_verdicts.why: The ALREADY_DONE verdict survives on substance — src/core/Sim.ts is built on FIXED_HZ from config/timing (meters stored as 1/FIXED_HZ integer units), core/rng.ts is mulberry32 pinned against a reference implementation in tests/rng.test.ts, tests/determinism.test.ts spawns two child vitest processes and requires byte-identical duel fingerprints across three processes, and the gate freezes states via DuelIntro.devHoldAt + scene.pause() + settleFrames. But one enforcement attribution is FALSE: tests/config-purity.test.ts contains no reference to randomness at all (grep -i random returns nothing in it or tests/utils/configPurity.ts); its checks are ZERO numeric literals in src/core/, import-graph restrictions, and unscannable-payload detection. No eslint no-restricted-globals rule bans Math.random either. The ban is a documented rule (src/core/CLAUDE.md 'No Math.random — inject Rng') plus a behavioural guard, currently honoured in fact (no Math.random anywhere in src/core/ outside comments) but not statically enforced.
item_verdicts.correction: Replace 'injected mulberry32 (no Math.random in core — enforced by tests/config-purity.test.ts)' with: 'injected mulberry32 — Math.random is banned in core by src/core/CLAUDE.md and caught behaviourally by tests/determinism.test.ts (cross-process byte-identical fingerprints) and tests/rng.test.ts, but NOT statically enforced: tests/config-purity.test.ts checks numeric literals and the import graph only, and no eslint rule bans it. If screenshot baselines come to depend on it, adding a Math.random scanner to tests/utils/configPurity.ts is a ~10-line genuinely additive gate.'

overall_note: Attacked all five items. Six cited URLs fetched (Chromium SwiftShader doc, chromestatus feature 5166674414927872 via page and raw API, playwright.dev/docs/test-snapshots, vitest.dev/blog/vitest-4, main.vitest.dev visual-regression guide, github.com/mapbox/pixelmatch) — all live, none fabricated, each broadly saying what is attributed to it. Two source-level errors found: the SwiftShader removal milestone is 139 (enterprise notice 131), not 130 (item 1); pixelmatch's perceptual metric is OKLab+HyAB, not YIQ (item 2). Repo side, every ADOPT/REJECT/ALREADY_DONE premise was re-derived from files: CI runs lint/test/build only, pre-commit is literally `npx vitest run`, vitest is ^4.1.10, the harness is DEV-only, gate data is committed while reference/ is gitignored, 55 = 40 config probes + 1 runtime probe + 14 scans, and all five canonical states exist in src/game/fidelity.ts. The single repo-level falsehood is item 5's claim that tests/config-purity.test.ts enforces the Math.random ban — it does not. No item cites a COMBAT_MEASUREMENTS.md row, so §00b and the §S24-H verify-pass corrections (HEAVY band 146–~275, A28 S3 cinematic-owned, 17-damage-on-draw / +309 px knockback, ASYM contested, ~616 px/s constant-speed dash) are orthogonal to this area and overturn nothing here. Net: the two ADOPTs and the REJECT stand, the ADAPT stands on stronger evidence than the research supplied (zero fighter-body probes in the fighting state), and the ALREADY_DONE stands with a corrected enforcement story.
